response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.account_id AS account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM "order" o JOIN account a ON a.account_id = o.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3), diff AS (SELECT account_id, region, order_count, order_count - AVG(order_count) OVER () AS diff_from_avg FROM c), r AS (SELECT *, AVG(diff_from_avg) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_avg_diff FROM diff) SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff_from_avg, diff_from_avg - region_avg_diff AS excess_over_region_avg FROM r WHERE diff_from_avg > region_avg_diff ORDER BY excess_over_region_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The overall average is the unweighted mean of order counts across all account–region rows (one row per account, since each account has a single branch district). The region average difference is the mean of the differences over all account rows in that region, computed before filtering.
Ties in the excess value are broken arbitrarily by the database, because the request gives no tie-break rule.
